evidence: CAP-03.S05.T03-R02-F01 is closed by verifying the complete immutable workflow-attempt capability inside the same SQLite writer transaction before either first candidate mutation or replay. Project, workflow run, job, step run, activity, concurrency class, attempt identity/number, worker, lease token/generation, idempotency key, and command fingerprint must match canonical job/attempt authority; the live-lease check remains additionally required for first commit.

Each one-field claim substitution fails with aggregate revision, provenance event, outbox event, attempt artifact, committed output, and workflow history counts unchanged. The exact claim atomically appends and completes once, while reopening the repositories and replaying the exact command returns the same candidate with all authority counts unchanged.

CAP-03.S05.T03-R02-F02 is closed by treating every durable non-informational dependency-impact item as adverse freshness authority inside the restoration BEGIN IMMEDIATE transaction. A prior adjudicated revision named by a started, partially checkpointed, failed-attempt, cancelled, recovered/completed, or overlapping durable change cannot be published as a false-fresh current revision before stale-cause materialization.

The real-SQLite suite proves all 13 requested immutable claim fields independently fail closed with no candidate, artifact, provenance/outbox, completion, or history write; it also proves exact initial commit and restart replay converge on the same candidate and durable receipt.

Restoration fixtures cover begin-before-advance after repository restart, partial checkpoint with an unmaterialized affected output, cancellation, two overlapping durable changes, injected failed-attempt audit, reopen/recovery to completed propagation, completed stale authority, and exact fresh restoration replay without rewriting history or orphaning propagation authority.

The remediation stays within the existing atomic selective-recalculation repository and aggregate UnitOfWork boundaries. Storage documentation now states that durable dependency-impact authority, rather than only a materialized stale-cause row, prevents fresh restoration.

No schema migration, public route, renderer, governed experience reference, package membership, external service, destructive operation, automatic adjudication, or unrelated product authority changed. The only additional production behavior is fail-closed validation at the two reviewed transaction boundaries.

verificationSelection.riskAnalysis: The complete open set is CAP-03.S05.T03-R01-F01 and its refined claimant-boundary finding CAP-03.S05.T03-R02-F01, plus CAP-03.S05.T03-R01-F03 and its refined in-flight-restoration finding CAP-03.S05.T03-R02-F02. reviewerDisposition.rootCauseAnalysis: R02 enforced canonical plan/output authority and liveness, but the first-write path reused the narrow active-lease lookup while the replay/completion path alone called the complete immutable claimant verifier. That asymmetry allowed caller-supplied fields to be persisted once and rejected on replay. Restoration similarly treated the derived stale-cause projection as the full freshness authority, overlooking the earlier durable impact-item decision recorded when propagation begins. R03 moves the already-existing complete claimant verifier ahead of both candidate paths and defines a durable impact item itself as adverse restoration authority, keeping both decisions inside their existing BEGIN IMMEDIATE transactions.
